args.title: Pipe coupling tightening
args.description: A threaded coupling sits on a pipe stub; insert it to the thread start then tighten clockwise to hand‑tight torque.

steps.description: Push the coupling onto the thread start until it seats on the chamfer.
Turn the coupling clockwise to hand‑tight torque.

assumptions: The coupling outer diameter is about 40 mm and length 45 mm.
Thread pitch is 1.5 mm, typical for 1‑inch pipe threads.
Seating depth is chamfer plus 3 mm.

insert_coupling: Threads are an approximation: a helical joint with a torque ramp; no thread flanks, cross-threading or galling. A screen, not a promise.
tighten_coupling: Threads are an approximation: a helical joint with a torque ramp; no thread flanks, cross-threading or galling. A screen, not a promise.

args.title: Cabinet maintenance
args.description: Unlock a quarter-turn latch, swing open a cabinet door, open a handwheel valve by a quarter turn, and insert an 8 mm test connector into a service port.

steps.description: Turn the quarter-turn latch counter‑clockwise to unlock the door.
Hook the door handle and pull the door open.
Turn the handwheel valve counter‑clockwise a quarter turn to open it.
Insert the 8 mm test connector into the service port.

assumptions: The latch requires about 0.5 N·m to turn and has a wing head 20 mm diameter.
The cabinet door is 400 mm tall, 200 mm deep, hinged on the left edge with a handle 20 mm from the front.
The service valve needs roughly 2 N·m to turn and has a 100 mm rim handwheel.
The test port socket accepts an 8 mm plug with 0.2 mm clearance and 1 mm chamfer.
Moved test_port from (0, -150) to (0, -240) mm to clear the swing of cabinet_door

unlock_latch: Latches are an approximation: a detent torque on a revolute joint; no cam or spring geometry.
open_valve: Valves are an approximation: a resistive torque curve on a revolute joint; no packing or seat dynamics.
